Title: The Singing Mine
Rumor: The Singing Mine. Prospectors speak of an abandoned silver mine from which a low, mournful song can be heard at night. Those who enter claim that the walls themselves hum with music, growing louder as they descend. One miner returned carrying a fist-sized crystal that continued singing for three days before shattering.
First lead: A disused mining trail beyond the Old Camp leads to the collapsed entrance.

Title: The Gate of Kar-Durim
Rumor: The Gate of Kar-Durim. Dwarven tradition holds that the ancient high gate of Kar-Durim remains standing somewhere in the mountains, its doors sealed since the fall of the Lost Holds. The gate is said to bear the names of every king who ruled within, and to possess mechanisms that no living smith can reproduce. Some claim that the doors open for a single hour each year.
First lead: Blackpick families preserve fragments of old maps describing the approach to the high gate.

Title: The Golden Mule
Rumor: The Golden Mule. A half-starved pack mule wandered into a mining camp carrying saddlebags filled with extraordinarily pure gold nuggets. No owner ever came forward. The animal repeatedly tried to return to the mountains but refused to follow any established trail, and its hooves bore traces of a strange black mineral.
First lead: The mule's former handlers left an account of its behavior at a prospectors' lodging house.

Title: The Chimneys of Thuldren Deep
Rumor: The Chimneys of Thuldren Deep. Highcairn storytellers describe narrow columns of smoke rising from inaccessible mountain slopes during the coldest winter nights. Some believe they emerge from the ancient foundries of Thuldren Deep, abandoned by the dwarves centuries ago. Others insist the smoke is proof that something still works the furnaces beneath the mountains.
First lead: Highcairn guides know the peaks from which the smoke is most often observed.

Title: The Miner's Lantern
Rumor: The Miner's Lantern. A yellow light occasionally appears deep within an abandoned working, moving slowly through passages long since collapsed. Prospectors claim it belongs to a miner who died searching for the richest vein in the mountains. Anyone who follows the light is said to discover gold, though not necessarily a way back to the surface.
First lead: The lantern is associated with an old prospect known as Widow's Cut.

Title: The King's Road Below
Rumor: The King's Road Below. Old dwarven songs describe a great subterranean highway connecting the Lost Holds, wide enough for six wagons to travel abreast. Sections supposedly remain intact beneath Blackvein's mountains, together with bridges spanning chasms that no living traveler has measured. A goblin salvager claims to have found one of its mile markers.
First lead: Cinderhook miners possess stone fragments bearing an ancient dwarven distance inscription.

Title: The Stone That Bleeds
Rumor: The Stone That Bleeds. Miners tell of a dark vein of rock that produces red liquid when struck with a pickaxe. The liquid resembles blood but hardens into a brittle mineral after exposure to air. Prospectors disagree about its value, while some Karrathi elves consider the deposit an omen warning against further excavation.
First lead: A disputed quarry near Karrathi territory reportedly contains the unusual stone.

Title: The Staircase Above the Clouds
Rumor: The Staircase Above the Clouds. Highcairn legends describe an ancient staircase carved into a sheer mountainside, ascending toward a summit usually concealed by clouds. The steps are far too large for an ordinary human, and their makers are unknown. A goliath tale claims that a visitor who reaches the top may ask one question of the mountain itself.
First lead: Oru Mountain-Song knows a traditional account identifying the mountain by its unusual twin peaks.

Title: The Lost Surveyor
Rumor: The Lost Surveyor. A surveyor vanished while mapping mineral deposits beyond the known claims. Months later, his field notebook was discovered beside a stream, containing careful drawings of a valley that no local guide recognizes. The final pages depict a strange tower standing among trees whose leaves appear to be made of stone.
First lead: The notebook passed through several hands before reaching a private collection in Blackvein.

Title: The Eyes in the Cavern
Rumor: The Eyes in the Cavern. Cinderhook miners avoid a certain cave system where hundreds of polished stones have been set into the walls. In lamplight, the stones resemble watchful eyes, and their arrangement supposedly changes whenever visitors leave the chamber. One goblin claims that placing a coin before the largest stone grants safe passage through the tunnels.
First lead: Cinderhook prospectors know the entrance but rarely discuss it with outsiders.

Title: The Blackpick King's Tomb
Rumor: The Blackpick King's Tomb. A dwarven family legend describes a richly furnished tomb concealed beneath a mountain shrine, containing the remains of a ruler who refused to abandon the ancient holds. The tomb's doors supposedly bear a warning that those who steal the king's possessions must return them before the third sunrise.
First lead: Borin Blackpick has heard competing versions of the tale, though none identifies the ruler with certainty.

Title: The Frozen Waterfall
Rumor: The Frozen Waterfall. During the deepest winter, a waterfall in the high mountains freezes into a great wall of blue ice. Behind it lies a cavern containing strangely preserved trees, animal bones, and objects from an age no one remembers. The cavern can reportedly be entered only while the falls are frozen.
First lead: Highcairn hunters sometimes use the frozen waterfall as a seasonal landmark.

Title: The Furnace That Never Cooled
Rumor: The Furnace That Never Cooled. Blackvein miners tell of a dwarven forge discovered inside an abandoned working. Though the surrounding chambers were cold and deserted, its hearth still glowed faintly, and a heavy hammer lay upon the anvil. The miners fled after hearing someone striking metal in a room they had just searched.
First lead: An old mine map marks the abandoned working with a crude drawing of an anvil.

Title: The Echoing Peak
Rumor: The Echoing Peak. There is a mountain where a shouted word returns not once, but seven times, each echo spoken in a different voice. Karrathi lore maintains that the mountain remembers every promise made upon its slopes. One old tale describes a warrior who climbed the peak to recover an oath forgotten by his ancestors.
First lead: Karrathi wardens recognize the mountain by an unusual split in its summit.

Title: The Glass Ravine
Rumor: The Glass Ravine. A remote ravine contains pools of smooth, dark glass formed by some tremendous ancient heat. Beneath the glass lie the shapes of trees, stones, and perhaps buildings, preserved as though frozen in place. Prospectors have recovered strange fragments there, but tools often break when they attempt to cut through the surface.
First lead: Cinderhook salvagers occasionally trade small pieces of the black glass in Blackvein.

Title: The Missing Claim Stakes
Rumor: The Missing Claim Stakes. Several prospectors report that their claim markers vanished overnight, only to reappear in a remote mountain hollow alongside dozens of markers belonging to mines abandoned decades earlier. Some accuse rival miners of an elaborate prank. Others insist the markers form a pattern visible only from the surrounding heights.
First lead: One of the displaced stakes bears a distinctive Ironmark assay stamp.

Title: The Mountain's Heart
Rumor: The Mountain's Heart. Highcairn legends speak of a chamber deep beneath the mountains containing a stone that beats like a living heart. Its rhythm can supposedly be felt through the soles of one's boots, and the surrounding passages shift with each beat. Some elders warn that removing it would bring down the entire mountain.
First lead: A Highcairn ceremonial song describes a cavern entrance shaped like an open hand.

Title: The Pale Lake
Rumor: The Pale Lake. Deep within the mountains lies a still subterranean lake whose waters shine faintly even in complete darkness. Travelers claim to see reflections of unfamiliar stars upon its surface, though no opening to the sky exists. A dwarven account describes a stone landing on its shore, where boats once waited for passengers who never returned.
First lead: An old Blackpick mining record mentions an underground waterway with similar properties.

Title: The Watchtower Without a Door
Rumor: The Watchtower Without a Door. A solitary stone tower stands upon a remote ridge, built in a style unlike any current Cadorian fortification. Its walls are smooth and unbroken, with no visible entrance at ground level. At sunset, a red light occasionally appears within the highest window, despite the tower having been abandoned for centuries.
First lead: The tower can reportedly be seen from a particular bend in an old mountain road.

Title: The Ledger of Durn Kharak
Rumor: The Ledger of Durn Kharak. Among the Lost Holds, Durn Kharak was said to preserve the records of ancient dwarven families and their possessions. Some believe that a portion of its royal archive survived the fall of the holds, containing the locations of forgotten mines, buried treasuries, and ancestral estates. If found, such records could transform the ownership of half the claims in the marquisate.
First lead: Dagna Flintmark has heard rumors of an old survey describing a route toward the lost archive.
